Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0009", "row_sha256": "280624c17315298ac924ac6d37eb55aae7e7eaf38cf49cad3f6f08405910f4f3", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you help clean up the english subtitles for the Lumen Parade show at North Pier Hall on october 18, 2025. its the full concert, not a trailer or highlights clip. i have one SRT export and the 1080p camera master at 25 fps, plus a board mix audio file. use the camera master to follow the actual picture and the board mix as the main reference for what is said and sung, though there are a few places where the crowd is louder than the mix. i need a revised SRT and a brief change log, not a review of the band's set or a summary of the concert.

please keep the subtitle file in english. dont translate anything or turn it into lyrics notes. preserve the existing cue numbers and the usual SRT numbering and timecode format. the current file has 246 cues and the last one is 00:58:41,200 --> 00:58:44,000. don't renumber cues just because a line is split or corrected; if you need to split a cue, keep the original number on the first piece and use the next available number for the added piece, then update later numbers only where needed to keep the numbering valid. the export has a few gaps and odd-looking line breaks, so please check those against the video rather than assuming every gap is a mistake. keep each cue readable on screen and don't let a caption cover the lower-left inset that shows the keyboardist.

one thing from the stage manager may change a section. if the production manager confirms that the venue cue sheet says the second encore began after 21:42:00, move cues 188 through 214 6.5 seconds later than their current times. if the production manager does not confirm that timing, leave cues 188 through 214 at their current times and mention the unconfirmed timing in the change log. those are the two options, not a reason to guess from the crowd reaction. if the first option applies, check cues 215 onward against the recording, but do not shift them automatically just because you moved the encore cues. the show video has a brief black frame at the end of the first encore, which could make the timing look different, so use the cue sheet confirmation for that specific decision.

for the spoken parts, keep the performers' wording and meaning, and don't tidy their grammar into something they didn't say. there are short introductions from vocalist Mara Vale, guitarist Tomas Iri, and drummer Niko Bell, but don't add speaker names to every caption. the file already has names on two introductions and those can stay where they're useful. please distinguish the three voices only when the audio makes that clear; don't guess which person is speaking from who is on camera, since a few lines are spoken off-screen. there is also a spoken line, “we can hear the river from here,” which should remain exactly as spoken if the audio supports that wording. if it doesn't, use what is actually audible rather than treating that line as confirmed by my note.

some words in the board mix are masked by applause, especially near the end of “Paper Satellites” and during the audience exchange before the encore. listen to the camera audio in those places as a secondary reference, but don't fill a gap from context alone. use [inaudible] only for speech that cannot be recovered from either recording, and don't add it for crowd noise or instrumental music. if two people talk over each other and both lines are clear enough, keep both without making up a speaker label. if only one can be understood, retain the recoverable words and flag the overlap in the change log, rather than replacing the whole cue. please don't silently remove a false start if it is audible; keep it when it affects the meaning, but a repeated syllable that is just a stumble can be cleaned up.

there's a lyric sheet from the band's label for “Paper Satellites” and “Lantern Teeth.” compare those two songs with the recording. when the words in the audio match the sheet, use the sheet's spelling and punctuation for the lyrics; when a sung line differs, follow the recording and don't force the sheet's version into the subtitle. the lyric sheet doesn't cover “Borrowed Weather,” so use only words that can be heard clearly for that song. retain the song titles exactly as listed here, including capitalization. don't add quotation marks around all lyrics, and don't insert a song title as a caption unless someone says it aloud.

there are a few visual cues too. the camera shows the handwritten sign “NORTH PIER / NO STAGE DIVING” during the walk-on, but it isn't spoken, so don't make a subtitle from the sign. at 00:31:08 the lights go out for about two seconds while the music continues; don't add a blackout description just because the picture is dark. keep any existing sound or music descriptions only if they convey something necessary, and use square brackets for descriptions that are already warranted. don't invent reactions, instruments, or stage directions from a still frame. where a description is needed for an audible event, make it short and place it in its own cue if there is room.

1. for the revised file, please check the following in order, but don't limit your review to only these points: spelling of names and song titles; whether the words match the recordings; cue in and out points; readable line breaks; and any accidental overlaps between captions. Mara's name is spelled Mara Vale, Tomas's is Tomas Iri, and Niko's is Niko Bell. the venue name is North Pier Hall. keep the punctuation natural for speech, rather than putting a full stop on every fragment, and use an em dash for an interrupted sentence only when the recording makes the interruption clear. don't change a question into a statement just to make a caption shorter.

please keep the captions to no more than two lines per cue. aim for around 42 characters per line, but don't split a name or a short phrase in an awkward place just to hit that number. there is no separate style guide beyond the details here, so don't introduce speaker IDs, sound labels, or capitalization rules that aren't needed. if a line is already accurate and readable, it can stay as it is. the subtitle file should remain synchronized to the video after edits, including after any applicable encore adjustment. the player sometimes displays the captions a little late on the preview, so assess timing against the master file itself rather than the preview window.

2. for the handoff, return the revised SRT as one complete file, followed by a short change log that names any meaningful corrections and notes any unresolved audio or timing issue. keep the log separate from the SRT so it can't be mistaken for a subtitle cue. don't claim a line was verified if the recording doesn't support it, and don't include a general concert recommendation. if the encore timing is not confirmed, say so in the log; if it is confirmed and cues 188–214 are moved, note that adjustment and that later cues were checked without being moved automatically. the final cue should still match the actual ending of the recording, not an assumed end time.

one last timing detail to check after the encore section: if the recording confirms that the audience calls “one more” before Niko says “thank you,” keep that order in the captions and align each line to the audio. if the recording does not confirm that sequence, follow the audible order instead and mention the discrepancy in the log only if it affects the edited captions. after the last spoken line, the recording has room tone before it ends, so don't extend the final subtitle across that silence. please keep this check in mind even if the earlier cue-sheet branch leaves the encore timings unchanged; it applies either way.", "output": "Please revise the English subtitles for the full Lumen Parade concert at North Pier Hall on October 18, 2025. Keep an audible false start when it affects meaning; a repeated syllable that is only a stumble may be cleaned up.
